pages.text:
Morgan Stanley
Interview Experience
Varun Sriram | T.Y.B.Tech CS 2022-26
Overview :
Two weeks before the Mid-Sem Tests, the Training and Placement Office
(TPO) forwarded a message about an on-campus drive by Morgan Stanley. It
was a complete surprise, as we hadn’t expected Morgan Stanley to come. The
online assessment was scheduled for the 10th of September, and the
interviews were on the 13th of September.
Eligibility Criteria:
1. Circuital Branch Student
2. CGPA ≥7.5
3. No Backlogs
Online Assessment:
An online Assessment was conducted on 10th September on the SHL
AMCAT Platform. There were three sections.
1.
Coding Section:
We had three questions to solve in 60 minutes.
Q1: I believe this problem involved N encrypted integers, requiring us to
decrypt them by multiplying the numbers together and expressing the
result as the product of distinct prime factors in ascending order. I was
stuck for about 20-25 minutes but managed to pass all the test cases.
Q2: This question seemed related to string manipulation. We had a string
of resource IDs representing system requests, focusing on important
letters (a, e, l, o, u). The task was likely to find the longest sequence of
these resources without repetition and count the requests, though the
details are a bit unclear.

Q3: I think this problem involved optimizing stage lighting for a play,
using an N x M matrix to represent light intensity, where positive values
indicated bright spots. The director had a maximum light intensity in
mind, and the goal was probably to identify sections that stayed within
this limit. I'm not entirely sure about the specifics.
2.
Debugging Section (20 mins):
●There was an option to choose your Java, C++ and Python.
●This Section involved 7 easy debugging questions.
●I was able to 6 questions completely.
3.
Aptitude Section (36 mins, 24 Qts.):
●This section was comparatively difficult, considering the time
allowed per question and the calculations involved in most of them.
●An important point to note is that it is crucial to attempt every
question, as it may be a deciding factor in selection. This applies to
every section, but for this particular section, it was challenging to
complete on time.
●I was also unable to attempt each question thoroughly; I randomly
marked the last few.
●The topics included permutations and combinations, task ordering,
statistics, and others.
This concluded the Online Assessment and the result was declared on 12th
September ( One day before the interview ).
23 students were shortlisted for interviews.

Interview:
The interview with Morgan Stanley was conducted online on Zoom which
started at 8 AM.
Round 1:
My interview was scheduled for 10 AM. There were two interviewers for the first
round. They began by introducing themselves, then asked me to introduce myself
(it’s always a good idea to have a well-prepared introduction, as it can leave a
strong impression on the interviewers).
First, they asked me a medium-level DSA question, which had two parts. I was
able to solve the first part and provide an idea for the second. The question involved
an integer array where each element represents the maximum jump that can be
made from that position. The goal of the first part was to determine whether it was
possible to reach the end of the array. The second part asked for the minimum
number of jumps required to reach the end of the array. I suggested that we could
use dynamic programming to solve this. Although I couldn’t derive the formula in
time, they seemed satisfied, and we moved on to the next questions.
The next question was on DBMS. They gave me a query to solve, which I was
able to handle successfully. In the follow-up, they asked about the execution order
of SQL queries (i.e., which clause is executed first among SELECT, FROM,
WHERE, etc.). Unfortunately, I couldn’t recall the correct order, which is a basic
concept. However, I made the right decision by not wasting the interviewers’ time.
After briefly trying to remember, I quickly admitted that I couldn’t recall the correct
order. They responded by saying, "No problem," and we moved on to the next
question.
The final question was about the four basic pillars of OOP, which I explained
clearly. Then, they asked if I had any questions for them. I asked two questions that
I had prepared in advance, ensuring that they demonstrated my interest in the role.
The interview lasted around one hour. Out of 22 candidates, 9 were selected to
proceed to the next round, and fortunately, my name was on the list.

HR Round:
This round aimed to assess my personality, strengths, weaknesses, capability
to handle the role, background, and overall fit for the job.
●First, the interviewer asked me to provide an overview of my resume or
summarize its contents.
●Next, he posed a straightforward DSA question, likely because I struggled
with a DSA question in my first interview. The question was to check
whether a given string is a palindrome.
●He then requested that I implement an OOP concept focused on the use
of abstract classes, assessing my understanding of the topic. A follow-up
question addressed the difference between overriding and overloading.
●After that, we transitioned to HR questions. He began by asking why I
wanted to work at Morgan Stanley (it’s essential to be prepared for such
questions).
●He also asked several situational questions, including:
o What would you do if there were differences of opinion within your
team?
o If you were working in the testing department and realized that
testing wouldn't be completed before the deadline due to numerous
edge cases, how would you communicate this to your boss,
considering they want to meet the deadline?
●He followed up with personal inquiries such as:
o What are your hobbies?
o Where do you live? Are you a local resident or a hostellite?
o How long does your commute take?
Finally, he asked if I had any questions for him. I posed a question, which he
answered, concluding the second round, the HR interview.
Results were announced at 8 PM. Out of 9 candidates, 8 were selected, and I
was fortunate to be among them.

Tips:
For Online Assessment:
●Practice questions from Geeksforgeeks and Leetcode. You can
also follow any sheet. for example - 450DSA by Love Babbar.
●Although It is not necessary but having some experience in Competitive
programming will give you an extra edge and you will be afraid of any
new questions you might get.
●If the test contains Aptitude questions, they generally include
Probability, PnC, Logic-based, Statistics, Math based puzzles, etc.
Practice some questions from the Geeksforgeeks or IndiaBix.
For Interview:
●Write down your introduction and try to remember it by heart.
●Be confident while answering the questions and remember if you
pronounced some words incorrectly or fumbled in between they will
not reject you for that.
●Be honest. if you don’t know a topic just let them know and
don’t mention projects, in your resume, that you haven’t worked
on.
●Also, in your resume, if you have mentioned any group project always
mention what did you do in particular.
●Whenever the interviewer asks you a question, make sure that you
understand the question correctly and I would suggest you that
repeat whatever you understand again so that the interviewer can
repeat the question again if you misunderstand something.
●While preparing for subjective topics like DBMS, etc. try to understand
things with real-world examples rather than mugging the definitions
and try to remember an example for each topic you learn.
●Go through some standard HR questions one day before the
interview so that you can be prepared for those questions.
●Stay hydrated during the interview.
●Believe in yourself.
●Don’t get demotivated by rejections, try to analyze what went wrong
and work on that part.

Resources:
●For DSA - GeeksforGeeks, Leetcode.
●For CP - Codeforces, Codechef.
●For OS - Gate Smashers playlist, InterviewBit-Questions.
●For DBMS - Gate Smashers Playlist, InterviewBit-Questions.
●For OOPS - GeeksforGeeks, OOPS by love babbar.
